values: I'll check your reservation.
I'm staying two nights, but booked each night separately. Can I have the same room?
Request the same room in Japanese for consecutive nights booked separately.
Do you have both reservation numbers?
Yes. The dates are consecutive, but the room types differ.
State both reservation numbers and explain in Japanese that the room types are different.
Staff will check availability and conditions.
I won't assume consecutive dates mean the same room; I'd like to ask the price difference too.
Ask in Japanese about the price difference without treating the same room as guaranteed.
If a change is difficult, you will need to move rooms.
In that case, please tell me how to store my luggage on the second day.
Ask in Japanese about luggage storage when changing rooms.
We'll check the fees and moving time together.
I'll decide after the explanation. Please don't cancel one booking first.
Say in Japanese that you want to hold off cancellation until after the explanation.
Staff will explain same-room availability and alternatives while keeping both bookings.
Is this to take away?
Yes. Could you split four buns into two bags of two?
Ask in Japanese for four buns divided into two bags.
Would you like two separate payments too?
I'll pay for everything together. I only want the items put in separate bags.
Distinguish separate bags from combined payment in Japanese.
Please tell me the items for each bag.
One sweet bun and one savory bread in each.
Specify each bag's contents in Japanese.
Is this combination correct?
Yes. My coworker and I are going home separately, so I'll check both bags' contents.
Say in Japanese that you will check both bags because you will go separately.
May I have the collection name?
Linh. Please keep it to these four without adding an order in my coworker's name.
Confirm the collection name and quantity without additions in Japanese.
We'll divide Linh's four items into two bags and take one payment.
Is this about photography?
The locker tag of the person beside me appeared in a photo I took for my own use.
Report in Japanese that someone else's tag appears in your private photograph.
Have you published or sent it?
Not yet. Rather than decide cropping solves it, I'd like advice on handling it.
Say in Japanese that it is unsent and you won't decide based only on editing.
Staff will check the location and photography rules.
It wasn't a changing area, but I'll also check whether photography is permitted here.
Check the location and photography permission in Japanese.
Please do not share other users' numbers with others.
I'll show only the necessary photo to staff and won't send it to friends.
Say in Japanese that you will show staff only what is necessary.
Until confirmation, please stop taking additional photos.
Yes. I won't publish it, and I'll ask about handling the saved image too.
Say in Japanese that you will stop further photography and ask how to handle the image.
I'll pass this on as an inquiry about an unpublished photo and its shooting location. Please refrain from photography now.
Check the person responsible before beginning work.
I heard a whistle, but it might have been a signal for the neighboring section.
Report in Japanese that you are unsure whether the signal belongs to another section.
Have you received instructions for your own section?
Not yet. I won't move materials based on the sound alone.
Say in Japanese that you have no instructions for your section and will hold work.
Let's check today's person responsible and work sheet.
I have the sheet. It says I'm responsible for transporting materials.
Show your assignment on the work sheet in Japanese.
Another team is working on the route.
I'd like to hear separately about the passage signal and work-start signal too.
Check passage signals separately from work-start signals in Japanese.
The supervisor will explain communication between the two sections.
After the explanation, I'll repeat the instructions for my assignment. For now I'll wait.
Say in Japanese that you will repeat instructions after the supervisor's explanation.
Keep waiting at the designated place. After the supervisor confirms, we'll give this section's instructions.
Are you having trouble with the name field?
My name is long, and the final two characters won't fit.
Say in Japanese that the end of your name will not fit in the field.
How does your identification show it?
My full name is shown on it. Please check it without shortening my name.
Show your unabridged identification details in Japanese.
I'll ask staff how to write it. Have you already submitted?
Not yet. I won't apply with an abbreviated entry.
Say in Japanese that you will hold off submitting an entry with your name shortened.
We'll investigate whether this is only screen display or a registration-field limit.
I don't know whether the display is just cut off either. I'd like to check the entered content.
Request in Japanese a check distinguishing display from registration limits.
We'll check the original document together with the input screen.
Please. I'll give my preferred form of address separately from my official full name.
Distinguish your preferred name from your official full name in Japanese.
I'll hand this over as an unsubmitted application. We'll explain how to register your official full name.
Do you need exit directions?
I'd like to go outside first, but my companion has my suitcase inside the ticket gates.
Say in Japanese that your luggage is with a companion inside the gates.
Where do you plan to meet your companion?
In front of the stairs on the same platform. If I leave alone, it seems I'd need to return to collect my luggage.
Explain the meeting place and problem of leaving first in Japanese.
Then meeting first sounds better. Do you know the exit you want?
The south exit. But I don't know the junction after going up the platform stairs.
Ask in Japanese about the turn toward the south exit.
On this map, south is right after the stairs. For large luggage you can use the elevator too.
I'll use the elevator after collecting my luggage. How do I get from the stairs to its entrance?
Ask in Japanese for the elevator route after collecting your luggage.
Go past the front of the stairs and toward the elevator sign farther down the platform.
Thank you. I'll first tell my companion the place, meet and take my luggage, then leave on the south side.
Say in Japanese that you will meet and collect luggage before heading for the exit.
Yes. Don't go through the gates first; collect the luggage and check the signs together.
Are you looking for the place in the photo?
Yes. I'd like to photograph this river view, but even on the same bridge, I can't see the building.
Ask in Japanese about the direction difference between the bridge photo and your view without the building.
Which way is the photograph facing?
I'm facing downstream now. The building in the photo might be upstream, but I don't know myself.
Explain in Japanese that you face downstream and the photo's direction is unconfirmed.
This photo uses the upstream side as its background.
Then I'll change direction. Rather than suddenly cross the road to the other side of the bridge, I'd like the pedestrian route.
Ask in Japanese for a route to face upstream without suddenly crossing the road.
Cross the bridge first, then change sides at the crossing farther ahead.
Understood. I won't insist on the exact photo position; I'll find a view along a route I'm allowed to use.
Say in Japanese that you will choose a photo spot along a route you can use, rather than insist on standing in exactly the same place.
When many people are passing, be careful where you stop too.
Yes. I'll move aside before photographing and check whether the upstream building appears. I won't stop other people from passing.
Say in Japanese that you will move aside and check the view and passage before taking photos.
You can change sidewalk sides using the route ahead. Choose the view direction separately from where you can stand safely.
Would you like advice about photographs?
When I photograph the night view, the lights behind me and my face reflect in the window. May I change position a little?
Describe the night-photo reflections and wish to change location in Japanese.
Do you have a tripod or similar equipment?
No, just my phone. I don't intend to stick anything on the window or turn off the lights.
Explain in Japanese that you have only a phone and won't alter the facilities.
The windows farther inside pick up less indoor light.
I'll move farther in. I'll choose an empty window so other people's faces don't appear.
Say in Japanese that you will choose a window where other people will not appear in your photo.
Will your companion move with you too?
Yes. If I start photographing first, we'll lose each other, so we'll confirm the place we're moving to together first.
Share your destination with your companion before moving in Japanese.
Don't put luggage on the passage side.
Understood. I'll hold my belongings and take photos briefly; even if reflections remain, I won't touch the facilities.
Say in Japanese that you will carry your belongings and photograph without touching the facilities.
Please do. The window farther in is on the right. Be aware of people passing while taking photos too.
Do you need help understanding explanations at today's appointment?
My friend will help me with Japanese explanations, but they have to return to work in thirty minutes.
Say in Japanese how long your interpreting friend can attend.
The consultation time isn't fixed yet. Is there anything you especially want to check yourself?
How to take the new medicine. I'd like an explanation that lets me take it correctly even after my friend leaves.
Request in Japanese medicine instructions you can understand after the appointment too.
The clinician will decide the medication. We can pass on your wish for written notes of the explanation.
Please. I'd like the frequency and times, and whether to take it together with my current medicine, written separately.
Request separate explanations of dose frequency and combined use in Japanese.
May we share the consultation information with your friend?
Yes, today's medicine explanation may be shared. There's no need to tell them all my unrelated past consultations.
Specify in Japanese the scope of information shared with your friend.
I'll tell staff that scope. Do you have information about your current medicines?
I have my medicine record book. I'm not requesting a guarantee we'll finish within my friend's available time; I'd like to discuss how explanations will work after they leave too.
Present the record book and ask in Japanese about explanations after your friend departs.
I'll take the book. I'll pass on the sharing scope and request for written explanation to the clinician.
What would you like to discuss today?
I handed in a wallet here yesterday. Later I remembered a landmark for where I found it.
Say in Japanese that you have additional information about the found item's location.
Do you have the receipt from the report?
Yes, this number. Yesterday I only said the park entrance, but realized there are two entrances.
Give the report number and explain the ambiguous entrance in Japanese.
Can you explain which entrance it was?
The side with the red bench. Not the road-side entrance, but where you enter from the riverside path.
Explain the bench and riverside position in Japanese.
Is there also a change to the time you found it?
The time is as I reported yesterday. Only the entrance location is what I want to add.
Clarify in Japanese that only the location information is changing.
I'll pass on the additional information. Have you been in contact with the wallet's owner?
No. Rather than look for the owner myself, I'd like to add accurate information to the record I submitted.
Request the record addition and say in Japanese that you won't search for the owner yourself.
I'll connect it to the report number and tell staff. If further checks are needed, we'll contact you using the details on the receipt.
reason: Repair confirmed English/Vietnamese naturalness and hint-clarity defects after complete scenario-context review; preserve all remaining source meaning and merge corrected canonical hints.
